RE: Formal Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Morgan Iverson
Member ID: W702529422
Reference Number: POC-1C4D453F27-72744
Date of Notice: 2026-07-31
Requested Service: Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
Ordering/Treating Surgeon: Duval, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the UnitedHealthcare Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 27130 (total hip arthroplasty), as set out in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-07-31, reference number POC-1C4D453F27-72744. This appeal is submitted within the 180-day window stated in that notice, which gives a deadline of 2027-01-27.

1. The stated reason for denial is not specific enough to respond to point-by-point.
The notice states only that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity" and that the determination was made "under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria." The notice does not name the policy, its number, or which specific criterion was not met. I am unable to identify which document this refers to with certainty. Based on my own research, the medical policy that appears to govern CPT 27130 for UnitedHealthcare Commercial/Individual Exchange members is titled "Surgery of the Hip" (Policy Number 2026T0503KK, the version currently published by UnitedHealthcare shows an effective date of September 10, 2026). Because that effective date is after the date of this denial, I ask UnitedHealthcare to confirm which version of this policy — including its policy number and effective date — was actually applied to this determination, and to provide me with a copy of it, as required for a full and fair appeal.

2. The policy text I was able to locate does not itself list the pass/fail clinical criteria for CPT 27130; it refers to InterQual criteria that I could not access.
The "Surgery of the Hip" policy states: "Surgery of the hip ... is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances. For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the: ... InterQual® Client Defined CP: Procedures: ... Removal and Replacement, Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Hip (AQS) (Custom) - UHG ... Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Hip (AQS) (Custom) - UHG. Click here to view the InterQual® criteria."

I have not been able to obtain the text of that InterQual criteria set myself — it is licensed content that is not published for public access — so I am not quoting or characterizing its specific requirements here, and I have not assumed what it requires. I respectfully request that UnitedHealthcare (a) identify, in writing, the specific InterQual element(s) it determined my record did not satisfy, and (b) provide me or Dr. Duval's office with the InterQual criteria document actually used, so that we can respond to the specific standard rather than a general one.

3. The clinical record supports medical necessity under the definitions UnitedHealthcare itself publishes in this policy.
While the specific InterQual checklist was not available to me, the "Surgery of the Hip" policy document does publish certain definitions that appear designed to operationalize that checklist. My record aligns with those published definitions as follows:

a. Radiographic osteoarthritis. The policy defines "Radiographic Findings of Osteoarthritis" as: "Narrowing of joint space, osteophyte formation, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral cysts, deformity of bony end plates, and thinning or complete loss of articular cartilage," and further states: "UHC will accept three or more moderate to severe radiographic findings to be sufficient to support the diagnosis of severe osteoarthritis."

The weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph obtained 2026-06-04 documents joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, subchondral sclerosis, and osteophytes — three of the enumerated findings, present on the affected hip. This meets the threshold UnitedHealthcare itself states it will accept as sufficient to support a diagnosis of severe osteoarthritis.

b. Disabling pain and functional disability. The policy defines "Disabling Pain" as a "Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Arthritis Index (WOMAC) pain domain of > 40" and "Functional Disability" as a "WOMAC functional limitation domain of > 40." A formal WOMAC score was not administered as part of this workup and is not in the current record; however, the clinical findings document the underlying functional and pain impairment those instruments are designed to capture: 12 months of progressive hip pain unrelieved by rest; pain and limitation severe enough that the patient ambulates with a cane, is limited to one block of walking, and cannot put on shoes unassisted; and exam findings of positive provocative testing on the affected side with range of motion limited by pain. [If UnitedHealthcare requires a formal WOMAC or HOOS score as part of its InterQual review, please advise, and Dr. Duval's office will arrange for one to be administered and submitted as a supplement to this appeal.]

c. Failed conservative treatment. The record documents a completed, supervised course of conservative management: 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (16 visits, 2026-05-13 through 2026-07-08) targeting hip abductor strengthening and gait, per the physical therapy discharge note; NSAID therapy for 6 months with inadequate relief; and an intra-articular corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-28 that produced only 3 weeks of partial relief. I am not aware of a published minimum conservative-treatment duration in the portion of the policy I was able to access, so I am not asserting that this satisfies a specific numeric threshold in the InterQual criteria — only noting that a substantial, supervised, multi-modality conservative treatment trial was attempted and failed before surgery was requested.

d. No disqualifying comorbidities. The record documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoker status. [If the applicable InterQual or policy criteria include specific BMI, infection-screening, or substance-use thresholds, please identify them; based on the values above, I do not believe they present a barrier, but I cannot confirm this without seeing the specific criteria.]

4. Requested action.
I ask that UnitedHealthcare:
(i) reverse the denial and authorize CPT 27130 for Morgan Iverson under the treating surgeon's plan of care; or, in the alternative,
(ii) provide the specific medical policy version (title, policy number, and effective date) and the specific InterQual criteria elements applied to this request, identify precisely which element(s) the submitted record did not satisfy, and allow a reasonable opportunity to submit additional documentation (including a WOMAC/HOOS score or other outcome measure, if required) addressing that specific gap before a final determination is issued.

Enclosed with this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-13 to 2026-07-08, 16 visits)
- Medication history documenting 6 months of NSAID use and corticosteroid injection dated 2026-05-28
- Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph and report dated 2026-06-04
- Clinical exam note documenting provocative testing and range-of-motion findings
- [Any additional records the surgeon's office wishes to include]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the name and contact information of the reviewer assigned to it. If a peer-to-peer review with Dr. Duval would assist the determination, please contact [surgeon's office phone/fax] to schedule one.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Morgan Iverson
